Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: single enemy sprite for a pixel-art 2D match-3 roguelike, drowned archive biome.
Style: ORIGINAL chunky 2D pixel art, as if drawn on a roughly 96x96 source pixel grid and enlarged with nearest-neighbor. Clearly visible hard square pixel clusters, no smooth gradients, no vector curves, dark brown almost-black 1-source-pixel outline, only 3–5 shades per material. Slightly grotesque cartoon cellar monster, charming but hostile. High silhouette readability at 160 pixels tall.
Composition: one single full-body creature in LEFT-FACING three-quarter battle pose, looking and attacking toward the LEFT side of the image, centered with generous transparent padding on all four sides, full extremities in frame. Square canvas.
Palette: cool dark teal, sea green, aged brass, parchment, occasional tiny coral accents.
Background and output: genuinely transparent background with actual RGBA alpha channel; all empty space fully transparent. No floor, no cast shadow, no ground, no pedestal, no backdrop, no text, no logo, no UI, no checkerboard, no border.

notes: All files are unchanged native image_gen PNGs, copied byte-for-byte. Seven RGBA sprites have genuine alpha. alpha_bbox measures every nonzero alpha pixel; visible_alpha_bbox measures alpha >16 to exclude nearly invisible native edge noise. All sprites face left; all battle arenas contain an empty continuous foreground walkway. archive-refuge native height is 940px; other arenas are 941px. No programmatic image editing was performed.
